title: A game developed using Emergent and Claude by Indie developer with minimum coding knowledge
author: casual_coder_525
selftext:
After months of building , I finally published my first android game on play-store and I’d love for you to try it.I have made use of various AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT etc are used in the process of developing this game. Especially Claude code helped me go through multiple iterations, solve bugs and even in preparing test scenarios.

Initial prototype was built using emergent and then developed it using Claude code. Idea churning is done using ChatGPT.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.krish0525.memorychess

🎨 Color-based memory gameplay — easy to pick up, hard to master    
👥 Designed for 2 players — great for friends & family    
🧠 Genuinely tests your memory and focus    
🚫 Completely ad-free (and free to download!)    
⚡ Quick rounds — perfect anywhere, anytime. Vehicle and Animal themes if you are bored with colors.

Feedback is welcome!

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body: Not OP. What makes glitch and itch worth putting out on if you're going to end up on Steam? I genuinely don't know what those platforms are.

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: For marketing, I would choose one audience before choosing channels. The clearest starting point looks like parents who want a quick two player memory activity with no ads. Record one fifteen second clip showing a complete round, then test separate hooks around family play, memory challenge, and no ads. I am building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) to help developers of agentically built games find players, run playtests, and keep people connected between versions. Memory Chess could use a small test group to sharpen the first session before broader promotion.
